sentences.text:
This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the
Act"), filed by the petitioners men
tioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose
. The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of LAC no. 198 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Anand Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 15 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

5. It is stated that the petitioners are only persons entitled to receive the compensation amount as per the actual prevailing market rate of the said land.
The actual physical possession of the said land has not been taken till the filing of the petitioner.
It is stated that the said award is not acceptable and the Award amount has been received under protest and without prejudice to their rights.
There is one Keekar tree aged about 10 years, and the same have became useless due to the acquisition of the said land in as much as the petitioners have also spent more than Rs. 10,000 on it.
The trees weigh more than 20 quintals and the rate of wood is @ Rs. 500 per quintal.

The NH 10 is 2 kms away from the said land,
the bottling plant of Indian Gas and FCI godown is around 3 kms from the said land, and Mundka,

It is also submitted that ld. LAC failed to appreciate that it is the distance and the potentiality of the land and not the village, which is to be kept in mind while awarding the compensation.

It is stated that the ld.
LAC failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10% yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.

10. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000 per square yards and that too only to hose who has applied for the LAC no. 198 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Anand Singh & Ors. v.

11. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money and the ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioners.
The ld. LAC has grossly erred in deducting the tax, as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.

It is stated that the petitioner is claiming the compensation for the said land @ Rs. 8000 per square yards and also entitled to compensation amount of Rs.

The petitioner also claims lumpsum amount of Rs. 1,00,000/ per acre along with interest for loss and damages.

17. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 25.05.2015 :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?

OPP 2. Relief.
18.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.

Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the LAC no. 198 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Anand Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 15 evidence led by them in case bearing Mukhtiyar Singh Vs.
Union of India, LAC No. 390 of 2016, Vill. Rani Khera.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
20. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
OPP 21.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
22.

sentences.text: Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

24. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

25. In the Mukhtiyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtiyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtiyar Singh (supra).

This court adjudicate the market value of land LAC no. 198 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Anand Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 15 of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
26.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 27.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).

(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
28.
Reference petition is accordingly answered.
All parties to bear their own respective costs.

Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the LAC no. 198 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Anand Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 15 evidence led by them in case bearing Mukhtiyar Singh Vs.
Union of India, LAC No. 390 of 2016, Vill. Rani Khera.
To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtiyar Singh (supra).
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
22.

There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtiyar Singh (supra).
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtiyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land LAC no. 198 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Anand Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 15 of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
26.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.

(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
28.
Reference petition is accordingly answered.
All parties to bear their own respective costs.
